item.title: Iran says US military not allowed to enter Gulf ‘under any circumstances’
item.description: Iran said on Saturday that US military ships would never be allowed to enter the Gulf “under any circumstances” and President Donald Trump will “take that dream to his grave”. The remarks came amid mounting US and Israeli threats of renewed attacks on Iran, as US ambassador to Turkey Tom Barrack warned that Washington could “absolutely” strike Iran as soon as this weekened. “We will not allow US military ships in the Persian Gulf under any circumstances and at any time,” said Iran’s armed forces chief of staff Ali Abdollahi, according to Iranian state television. “The US president must dream of seeing the armed forces enter the Persian Gulf. He will take that dream to his grave.” Iranian forces have restricted traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, a vital energy conduit and gateway to the Gulf, since the war with the United States broke out on February 28. In retaliation, the United States has imposed a counterblockade on Iranian ports and ships. Tehran has required vessels to seek permission to transit, and repeatedly targeted ships attempting to pass through Hormuz via a southern route close to the Omani coast. According to the Guards, several tankers attempting to transit Hormuz through the route Tehran considers “illegal” were hit by mines in recent days. On Friday, the Guards said two supertankers carrying more than 4.5 million barrels of crude oil have been abandoned at sea after hitting mines in the strategic waterway. “Their engine rooms were disabled by an explosion and a fierce fire,” the Guards said in a statement carried by their Sepah News website. In peacetime, around a fifth of the world’s oil and gas passed through Hormuz. AFP The post Iran says US military not allowed to enter Gulf ‘under any circumstances’ appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Why some people in Tinubu’s govt don’t want Fashola around – Laolu Akande
item.description: Former presidential aide, Laolu Akande, has alleged that some people around President Bola Tinubu do not want former Minister of Works and Housing, Babatunde Fashola, in the current administration because he would not tolerate certain practices within the government. Akande said Fashola’s absence from the government could partly be due to fatigue but argued that the opposition of some people around Tinubu was a more significant factor. He spoke during an interview on the Naija Unfiltered Podcast, where he also discussed Tinubu’s government and the perceived fallout between the president and former Vice President Yemi Osinbajo. Akande, who served as Senior Media Aide to Osinbajo under former President Muhammadu Buhari, described Fashola as someone who would not compromise his principles to accommodate those around him. “I think the reason why Fashola is not in this government, two reasons. I think Fashola himself has a bit of fatigue, more importantly, I think there are people around the president who don’t want to see Fashola because Fashola is not going to tolerate many of those things that you are seeing around,” he said. Akande added that Fashola was known for standing his ground, suggesting that his disposition might have made some people in the president’s circle uncomfortable. “Whatever you say about Fashola, he doesn’t take nonsense and the people who wanted to get some nonsense going, they didn’t want Fashola,” he said. The former presidential aide, however, said Fashola remained close to Tinubu and had not had a major public disagreement with the president. He suggested that, despite the absence of an open confrontation, there could be underlying tensions between the two politicians. “Even somebody like Fashola, who is still very close to the president — no problems openly, although they are also under current which he will speak about, but at least he didn’t have any blowout problem with the man,” Akande said. He maintained that some people around Tinubu did not want individuals like Fashola in the administration for reasons beyond the former minister’s own reluctance to return to government. Fashola served as governor of Lagos State from 2007 to 2015 before joining Buhari’s cabinet, where he was first appointed Minister of Power, Works and Housing and later served as Minister of Works and Housing. He has not held a position in Tinubu’s administration. The post Why some people in Tinubu’s govt don’t want Fashola around – Laolu Akande appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Uyo remains home ground for Super Eagles for now
item.description: The Nigeria Football Federation is not ready to move the Super Eagles’ home games from Uyo to Lagos, with a senior official saying Lagos is under consideration but Uyo stays the venue for now. The comments followed the Super Eagles’ 3-0 loss to Guinea-Bissau in an AFCON 2027 qualifier. Nigeria have three points from two Group L games, while Guinea-Bissau lead the group on six, the outlet said. It was earlier reported that the Super Eagles could host November qualifiers in Lagos. But the renovated Teslim Balogun Stadium is not yet ready to host an international. NFF inspectors will visit once the Lagos State Government finishes the renovation. The federation is also considering friendlies at Teslim Balogun to test the facilities and gauge the reaction of fans, and plans to consult players before deciding, the report said. The official argued that changing a settled home ground could hurt performance. The Super Eagles have played most of their home games in Uyo for nearly a decade. The NFF’s stated reasoning is cautious, and the logic is easy to follow: a stadium that has not been inspected cannot host a qualifier. The harder question is the calendar. With less than a month to the November double-header against Tanzania, there is little room for inspections and approvals if Lagos were chosen. If the stadium is not signed off in time, Uyo is the only practical option for the next home game, whatever the appetite for change. If it is, the NFF has said it would test the venue with a friendly first, which suggests a move for a competitive match would come later rather than sooner. The final say goes to 100 specialist journalists, one from each of the top 100 FIFA-ranked nations for the men’s award, and 50 for the women’s award as of September 8, 2026. Each juror names his Top 10 in order. This year the competition is different. Never in recent memory has the queue been this long, this loud. Not two. Not three. Five, six, seven men with a legitimate shout, a season to point to, a trophy to hold up. No one has blown the field away. No one can say, “It is mine.” And yet, with days to go, one must go home wearing the most prestigious hat in football. Start with the favourite, Harry Kane. No footballer in the world scored more in 2025/26 than Kane – 61 goals for Bayern Munich, 36 in the Bundesliga to win his third straight Torjägerkanone and a second European Golden Shoe. He delivered a domestic treble – Bundesliga, DFB-Pokal and the Franz Beckenbauer Supercup. If I was voting, I will vote for Harry Kane. His moment? April was brutal and beautiful. 100 Bundesliga goals in record time, then that semi-final vs PSG where he scored twice but Bayern went out 6-5 on aggregate. At the World Cup he led England to bronze with 6 goals, including a 6-4 thriller against France in the third-place playoff. Could he be the first English winner since Michael Owen in 2001? Then Kylian Mbappe – football’s ultimate World Cup man. 38 goals in 33 games for Real Madrid before the tournament, winning the Pichichi. Then in America, 10 goals to become the World Cup’s all-time top scorer at just 27. He is now the first player in history to win the Golden Boot in the Champions League, La Liga and the World Cup in the same calendar year – a treble of scoring crowns that may never be broken. His moment was not lifting the trophy – France finished fourth – but the way he left it all on the pitch. A breathtaking opener against Senegal to get his World Cup account going, a hat-trick vs Norway in the group stage, and four assists on top of the 10 goals. 22 goals in 22 games across three World Cups is the story of greatness. He did not win the World Cup, but he won history. Lamine Yamal is so many people’s favourite. He and Olise at the highest level are the most entertaining footballers in the game at the moment and he already has an archive of breathtaking goals. At 19, he could become the youngest Ballon d’Or winner ever, a record held by the great Ronaldo Nazario who won it at 21 years and 96 days in 1997. Yamal’s story writes itself: La Liga champion, La Liga Player of the Year, and then World Champion with Spain. His tournament was quiet by his standards, but he contributed to Spain’s victory which was largely a team performance. He completed 27 dribbles from 51 attempts – the highest total at the World Cup. He was Man of the Match twice, against Austria and Belgium in the semi-final – a game in which Spain were underdogs – and he won the crucial penalty that gave Spain the opening goal. For Barcelona this past season: 24 goals and 17 assists, averaging a goal contribution every 85 minutes. He is no longer the future. He is the present. If Yamal is the present, Michael Olise is pure magic. Bundesliga Player of the Season with numbers that read like a video game – 15 goals, 19 assists in the league, 22 goals and 31 assists in 52 games across all competitions. Two moments define him. First, the Freiburg game: Bayern down 0-2, Olise scores two and assists three in a 6-2 comeback. Then the quarter-final vs Real Madrid – 90+3, 4-3 on the night, that left-foot curler past Lunin to send Bayern through. At the World Cup he broke Pelé’s record with 7 assists in one tournament for France. As Thomas Müller said, “He has that dance-like, artistic ease you can’t learn.” And then Lionel Messi. At 39, in what might be his last World Cup, he took Argentina to the final and lost 1-0 to Spain in extra time. Heartbreak in New Jersey. He was Player of the Tournament until the final against Spain. He single-handedly dragged Argentina to the World Cup final in a manner that clearly stood him apart from the pack. But look at what he still did: 25 goals and 15 assists for Inter Miami this season, first player ever to record 15+ assists in three straight MLS seasons, first to have 30+ goal contributions in three different seasons. His moment? October 17th vs Atlanta – two goals, one assist, his 934th career goal. He is chasing a third straight MLS MVP. He is 39 and still top-two in the Golden Boot race. The defending champion Ousmane Dembele wants back-to-back. PSG retained both Ligue 1 and the Champions League, and Dembele was again their engine – 20 goals in the league campaign, 7 in the Champions League. His best moment came in the World Cup quarter-final run – 6 goals including that hat-trick against Norway. France faded late, but Dembele proved last year’s Ballon d’Or was no fluke. Can he retain it? Rodri is the anomaly. He left Manchester City for Barcelona this summer after winning the World Cup Golden Ball. Spain’s captain, the metronome who made Spain champions again. His moment wasn’t a goal, it was control. In the final against Argentina, with Messi throwing everything at Spain in extra time, Rodri won the ball back 11 times and completed 96% of his passes. The anchor. The man who makes everyone else look good. So who does the cap fit? If you want pure numbers, it’s Kane. If you want trophies, it’s Yamal. If you want history, it’s Mbappe. If you want beauty, it’s Olise. If you want longevity, it’s Messi. If it was just about who was the best player at the World Cup, Rodri has a real shout – World Cup winner and Golden Ball winner. On October 26th at the London Palladium, football will finally have to choose. For once, there is no wrong answer – only a hard one. For much of his early career, Alex Iwobi was often viewed as a talented but inconsistent player. Critics questioned his end product, while supporters saw flashes of brilliance that hinted at something greater. The amazing thing is that football careers are rarely linear. Now at Fulham F.C., the Nigerian midfielder appears to be experiencing something of a renaissance. His recent performances suggest a player who has matured tactically, refined his decision-making, and become one of the most dependable midfield engines in the Premier League. From Arsenal Prodigy to Premier League Mainstay Born in Lagos, Nigeria, Iwobi moved to England at a young age and joined the academy of Arsenal F.C. at just six years old. During his Arsenal years, he was primarily deployed as a winger or attacking midfielder, often tasked with linking midfield to attack. Work Rate Across his Premier League career he has recorded about 330 tackles, 144 interceptions and 147 clearances These contributions underline his transformation into a complete midfielder rather than a purely attacking player. Another measure of Alex Iwobi’s evolution is his longevity in one of football’s most competitive leagues. Often operating behind attacking stars like Victor Osimhen and Ademola Lookman, his creativity helps link midfield control with attacking penetration. item.title: Edo govt, NLC strike peace deal as Labour moves to restore electricity
item.description: By Victor Ahiuma-Young The Nigeria Labour Congress, NLC, and the Edo State Government have resolved their prolonged dispute, with the state government agreeing to recognise the NLC caretaker committee. As part of the truce, the National Union of Electricity Employees, NUEE, is expected to take steps towards restoring electricity to the state that has been in total darkness since Monday. The NLC Acting General Secretary, Benson Upah, said the resolution followed a meeting brokered by the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, SGF, at his residence on Friday, October 23, 2026. item.title: 21-year-old butcher stabs colleague’s to death in Ogun
item.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Ogun State Police Command has arrested a 21-year-old butcher, Selim Ayodele, over the alleged stabbing to death of his 26-year-old colleague, Ibrahim Wasiu, following a disagreement at their workplace in Alagbole, Ogun State. Read Also: Family seeks justice as butcher hacks 25-year old wife to death in Ekiti The incident reportedly occurred on Sunday, October 18, 2026, after the two men had finished work at a cow meat-selling outlet. In a statement issued on Friday, the Police Public Relations Officer of the command, DSP Oluseyi Babaseyi, said the incident was reported at the Ajuwon Police Station at about 8 p.m., prompting a police response. According to the police, preliminary investigations revealed that the disagreement between the two colleagues arose over who should sweep the floor after the day’s work. The statement alleged that during the ensuing altercation, Ayodele picked up a knife and stabbed Wasiu in the left side of his chest before twisting the weapon. The victim was subsequently rushed to Life Hospital, where he was confirmed dead on arrival. His remains were deposited at Life Channel Private Mortuary, Lanbe, Ajuwon, pending an autopsy, the police said. The police added that the suspect was in custody as investigations continued ahead of his prosecution. The Commissioner of Police in Ogun State, Bode Ojajuni, reaffirmed the command’s commitment to responding promptly to criminal incidents, conducting thorough investigations and ensuring the lawful prosecution of suspects. He also urged residents to exercise restraint when disagreements arise, resolve disputes peacefully and promptly report criminal incidents to the police. The command reiterated the importance of peaceful conflict resolution, warning against allowing minor disagreements to escalate into violence. His strict adherence to artistic excellence on-screen and his constructive roles in industry leadership, including his service to the Actors Guild of Nigeria, helped shape the positive trajectory of Nollywood. “His recognition as a United Nations Ambassador of Peace further highlighted his commitment to using his creative platform for the betterment of society. The consequential raid ordered by the federal government revealed deeper than anticipated. Fighting one threat exposed another. Though the authorities are shy of talking about it, the military operation reportedly uncovered booming trade in gunrunning, hard drugs and brothels during the demolition. Security sources referenced 40 AK-47 rifles and other ammunition allegedly recovered, with some persons including the market leader reportedly arrested. Brigadier General Ibrahim Baba Buhari, Commander 63 Brigade Asaba and Commander Sector 1, South-South, Operation Delta Safe, was not forthcoming with official position. Neither was the Commanding Officer at the 3 Battalion. But top military sources who spoke behind camera gave insight into the underworld the Effurun Mammy had become. One senior officer explained the procedure for high-profile suspects when Vanguard sought response from relevant military formations in Delta. “If we have caught some people with rifles, that means they are high-profile suspects, right? And, in our mandate, they are not meant to stay with us for a very long time. As soon as we finish our investigation, we hand them over to police, is that so?” He added he was not directly in charge of the market: “I’m just hearing what you’re telling me now. I have to make my own findings also. Me, I’m in the Brigade, not in the sector. And the Mami Market is under the CO 3 Battalion, not under the Brigade or sector.” Another security source who monitored the demolition was more direct about what Mammy harboured: “The location is Uburoko, just right behind the Mami Market. Those are also inside the barracks, that’s where those brothels are, inside the Mammy. “So, that’s where they hide after vandalizing those pylons. So, that people lose electricity, and the national grid is down, it’s because of actions like this.” He said the adjoining scrap market is the real enabler that must be shut: “There’s a need for the scrap market to be scrapped. Otherwise, they are all looting to the scrap market, and the vandalization or vandalism will continue. “Government should close downthat scrap market, because nothing good ever happens out of a scrap market. They call those scrap markets ‘One Naija,’ ‘One Sambisa’. “Once they (stolen power line assets) enter there, under five minutes, they have it dismantled, it’s melted. They harbour them, you can’t separate good people from bad people.” He said vandalism started in December 2025 but became unbearable in August 2026 when 11 pylons were brought down after vandals cut smaller components to weaken the structure. One vandal died when a weakened tower collapsed on him. “That picture of the dead person, he didn’t know the pylon rods had become weak from initial scavenging. So as he was cutting the pipe, the thing just came down on him.” He warned eviction alone will not work because displaced vandals are relocating to a dump site across the road, stressing that police, NDLEA and other agencies find it difficult to enter Mammy because it is taken as a military zone. “The Police, NDLEA and other security agencies, they find it difficult to penetrate and enter (the Mammy) because they take it as a military zone so most of them (vandals) seek safe haven in Mammy.” He defended the operation was not a raid: “We were not even raiding. We were just demolishing. So they are entering, picking their things and leaving. We are not beating anybody, not restricting them.” He said TCN is exhausted by the cost and delay of replacement. “TCN got tired. The one in Delta cannot repair those pylons. They have to get it from outside and it takes months. Just compare the amount of energy being lost to vandals.” Visual evidence shows catastrophic damage – total structural failure of towers like T98 and T100 after systematic stripping of base bracing, angle iron, bolts and gusset plates. TCN’s patrol on Delta/Afisere 132kV line found nine towers – T9, T10, T11, T12, T14, T15, T16, T17 & T18 – vandalised and needing urgent rehabilitation to avoid collapse. Not An Isolated Case The pattern is not limited to Delta. In Rivers State, advocate Alhaji Brian Barile who documents vandalism from Afam Power Plant, Oyigbo to Elelenwon in Obio/Akpor said: “From Elelenwon to Oyigbo, all the base braces and components of the electricity towers are gone, all stolen.” He described what he met around Green City Estate: “I was on the railway from Elelewon to Ogba side doing some work when I decided to stroll within Elelewon, under the Green City Estate, around the designated International Cattle Market when I discovered the mind-boggling vandalism.” Comparing untouched and vandalised towers, he said, “I saw one (pylon) untouched because there are living houses surrounding. You can see it’s complete, untouched, formidable and giving the pylon strength to stand.” “Others have been compromised, vandalised. They’ve everything at the base removed and you can see the pole (mast) bending. Anything can happen now. The strength of these poles are gone.” For TCN, the bulldozers in Mammy were not just about land. It was a desperate push to save the national grid from a dark economy of scrap, arms and drugs thriving behind barracks gates. For the law-abiding among thousands of squatters evicted from the Mammy, the bulldozers also left in their trail huge human cost in loss of property and livelihoods many would take who knows how long to recover from. Showunmi was the spokesman for Atiku Abubakar’s presidential campaign in 2019. If Nigerian politics were a church, these two would have explaining to do about their conversion. Showunmi’s declaration that prosperity is around the corner makes the issue particularly urgent. Nigerians have spent years hearing explanations for hardship, assurances that reforms will eventually pay off, and promises that the pain of today is the price of a better tomorrow. The market woman still calculates what she can afford before buying food. The worker still watches transport fares swallow a growing share of his salary. Parents still struggle with school fees, rent, electricity bills, and the cost of keeping a household running. For millions of people, the corner called prosperity has become a destination repeatedly announced but never quite reached. Showunmi is entitled to believe Tinubu deserves another term. But he must do more than announce that better days are approaching. He should tell Nigerians what evidence supports his optimism, what tangible improvements they should already see, and when the promised relief will begin to make a difference in their lives. Welcome to the Nigerian political marketplace, where the occupants change rooms, the promises acquire fresh packaging, and yesterday’s sworn enemies discover they have always shared common ground. The cost of this arrangement is not merely the embarrassment of watching familiar faces defend unfamiliar positions. It is the steady erosion of public trust. When political arguments change with the fortunes of the people making them, citizens have reason to question whether they are hearing honest assessments of the country’s problems or simply the latest sales pitch from a campaign office. Showunmi and Bwala need not apologize for leaving Atiku’s camp. They do, however, have an opportunity to demonstrate that their present positions rest on more than the convenience of political realignment. They can explain what they believe Tinubu has done right, address what he has done wrong, and make a credible case for why another term would serve Nigeria’s interests. As 2027 approaches, the country will be crowded with people eager to explain why their preferred candidate deserves power. Some will have remained loyal to one camp for decades. Others will have traveled through several parties, alliances, and campaign offices. Voters should judge each argument on its merits, but they must not be expected to forget the history of the people making it. Nigerians are not an audience to be entertained between elections, nor are they customers obliged to buy whatever a familiar salesman places before them. They have to live with the consequences of political decisions long after campaign slogans have faded and spokesmen have moved on. Showunmi can tell Nigerians that prosperity is near. The judgment belongs to the people listening. THE QUEST FOR NATIONAL INTEGRATION Following the end of the Nigerian Civil War in 1970, the urgent questions of national reconstruction, reconciliation, and the restoration of confidence among the country’s diverse peoples occupied a central place in political discourse. These concerns became particularly prominent during the formation of political parties in 1978, as Nigeria prepared for a return to civilian rule. The political parties recognised, to varying degrees, the need to accommodate the country’s complex ethnic and regional composition. The National Party of Nigeria (NPN), which eventually won the presidential election, adopted a political arrangement that reflected the importance of balancing interests across the North and the South in the distribution of key political offices. It was within this political atmosphere that Dr. Alex Ekwueme emerged as the NPN’s vice-presidential candidate, alongside Alhaji Shehu Shagari as its presidential candidate. The significance of the Igbo presence in the vice-presidential calculations of the major political parties of the period deserves particular attention. With the exception of the Nigerian People’s Party (NPP), whose presidential candidate, Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe, chose Professor Ishaya Audu as his running mate, the other major parties also featured Igbo politicians as their vice-presidential candidates. These choices were politically significant. At the very least, they reflected an awareness of the need to broaden the political coalitions upon which the Nigerian federation rested and to reassure the Igbo people that, despite the devastation of the Civil War, they remained an integral part of the Nigerian project. It would, however, be a mistake to regard these political arrangements as merely symbolic. They raised a fundamental question about the future of Nigeria: could the country achieve genuine reconciliation and lasting unity without creating a political environment in which every major ethnic and regional group had a fair opportunity to participate in national leadership? The prospect of an Igbo man ascending to the presidency subsequently became a subject of considerable political sensitivity. The lesson is unmistakable. National unity cannot be sustained by rhetoric alone. It requires deliberate political arrangements, mutual trust, and a willingness to accommodate the legitimate aspirations of all sections of the country. He was subsequently detained by the military authorities and subjected to imprisonment. The consequences were particularly troubling for what is today the South-East geopolitical zone, whose concerns about representation and its relative position within the federation have remained important elements of the national debate. The point is not that every administrative or political change undertaken under military rule was necessarily designed to disadvantage a particular region. Rather, it is that institutional arrangements introduced without sufficient regard for fairness, transparency, and the confidence of all constituent groups can deepen existing grievances and undermine national cohesion. The failure of the Babangida administration to complete a credible transition to democratic rule, culminating in the annulment of the 12 June 1993 presidential election, further aggravated the national crisis and deepened public distrust of the political process. That concern places responsibility on several institutions. Agencies that provide personnel must keep reliable records and protect their recruitment processes. INEC must scrutinise the names it receives, verify identities and supervise workers on election day. Political parties and their agents, meanwhile, have a role in observing the process and raising concerns through proper channels. Igini said INEC’s senior officials would not be present at every polling unit on election day. The work would be carried out by temporary staff under the commission’s supervision, making the quality of that supervision central to the process. He also noted that party agents and voters could help monitor what happens at polling units. His argument is that accountability should not end with the recruitment of workers. The public needs confidence that the people managing the vote are the people selected for the job, that they have been properly trained and that their actions can be checked. item.title: Ebola Vaccine Trial Begins In DR Congo – WHO Chief
item.description: The first clinical trial of an Ebola vaccine in the outbreak gripping the Democratic Republic of Congo began Friday, the head of the World Health Organization said. The DR Congo’s worst-ever Ebola outbreak has passed the 9,700-case mark, with the number of deaths exceeding 4,600. Among the many challenges facing the response is the lack of any approved vaccines or treatments for the Bundibugyo species of Ebola behind the epidemic. A health official works in the laboratory extraction room of the Institute of Lassa Fever Research and Control in Irrua Specialist Teaching Hospital in Irrua, Edo State, midwest Nigeria, on March 6, 2018. Photo by PIUS UTOMI EKPEI / AFP Ervebo, a vaccine approved for use against the more common Zaire strain of Ebola, will be put through a full-scale human trial in the DRC to see if it offers any cross-protection against Bundibugyo. “Science gives us hope. Today, in Bunia, DRC, the first participants were vaccinated in a new Ebola vaccine trial called Tumaini, which means ‘hope’ in Swahili,” WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said on X. “This trial will help us understand whether any of the vaccine candidates designed for Bundibugyo virus work. “In the meantime, the existing Everbo vaccine (licensed for use in preventing other Ebola virus disease) will be tested. “WHO is supporting this DRC-led effort to find answers and save lives.” The so-called Tumaini trial in the DRC — a single trial framework that can test the safety and efficacy of multiple vaccines — should also eventually incorporate two Bundibugyo-specific candidate vaccines, which are moving through earlier-stage, smaller-scale clinical trials. One is a ChAdOx1 adenoviral vector jab being developed by the University of Oxford; the other, by the US-based Moderna group, uses mRNA technology. item.title: Enugu Rangers Crash Out Of CAF Champions League After Late Collapse To MC Alger
item.description: Nigerian champions Rangers International of Enugu crashed out of the CAF Champions League on Friday after losing 3-0 to Algeria’s MC Alger at the Ali La Pointe Stadium in Algiers. The defeat handed Rangers a 3-2 aggregate loss, despite their 2-0 victory over the Algerians in the first leg in Abeokuta last weekend. The Flying Antelopes failed to protect their advantage, succumbing to late pressure as MC Alger scored three unanswered goals to secure a place in the group stage. After a goalless first half, MC Alger needed three goals in the remaining 45 minutes to overturn the deficit and keep their campaign alive. Enugu Rangers defender tries to stop MC Alger attacker in CAF Champions League game in Algiers on Friday, October 23, 2026. Photo Credit: CAF Online The comeback began in the 58th minute when Chahreddine Boukholda put the hosts ahead, raising hopes among their supporters. With six minutes left in regulation time, Guinean forward Mohamed Bangoura scored MC Alger’s second goal to level the tie at 2-2 on aggregate, sparking celebrations in the stands. As the match appeared to be heading for a penalty shootout, Soufiane Bayazid struck three minutes into stoppage time to complete MC Alger’s comeback and seal a 3-0 win on the night and a 3-2 aggregate victory. The result ended Rangers’ bid to reach the group stage, while MC Alger will now seek to advance further in the competition as they pursue a second continental title, 50 years after winning it in 1976. item.title: Nigeria’s Power Minister Commissions 120MVA Transmission Substation In Katsina
item.description: Katsina State has recorded another major milestone in its quest for improved electricity supply as the Minister of Power, Joseph Olasunkanmi Tegbe, and Governor Dikko Umaru Radda commissioned the newly completed 120 MVA, 132/33 kV Transmission Substation in Kankia Local Government Area. Speaking at the commissioning ceremony on Friday, the Minister described the project as a key component of the Federal Government’s strategic efforts to strengthen Nigeria’s national grid and expand electricity transmission capacity across the country. He reaffirmed President Bola Tinubu’s administration’s commitment to delivering critical power infrastructure that will ensure electricity generated across the country is efficiently transmitted to homes, businesses and industries. Governor Dikko Radda hailed the completion of the substation as a landmark investment in Katsina’s power infrastructure, noting that the facility, equipped with two 60MVA transformers with a combined capacity of 120MVA, will significantly reinforce the state’s transmission network and enable greater volumes of electricity to reach consumers. Radda stressed that reliable electricity remains the backbone of economic growth, industrialisation and improved public service delivery, adding that the project will complement Katsina’s expanding renewable energy programme while boosting key sectors such as agriculture, agro-processing, commerce, education and healthcare. Governor Radda expressed appreciation to President Tinubu for approving the project and commended the Minister of Power and the Transmission Company of Nigeria for ensuring its successful completion. He also urged residents of the host community to safeguard the facility against vandalism, describing it as a strategic national asset that will serve present and future generations. item.title: INEC Legally Bound To Publish Voters’ Register Online – Itodo
item.description: The Executive Director of Yiaga Africa, Samson Itodo, says the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) is legally required to publish the voters’ register online ahead of the 2027 general elections. Itodo’s position follows calls by opposition politicians and civil society groups for the electoral body to make the register available online. Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Friday, he said the demand was backed by Section 19 of the Electoral Act 2026, which provides for the publication of the register both at designated physical locations and online. “I think on this point about the release of the voters’ register, the law is very clear in Section 19 of the 2026 Electoral Act that after voter registration, there is claims and objections and that claims and objections shall happen not later that 90 days, in other words, it can happen earlier than 90 days but not later than 90 days before the day of an election. And what will be the mode? First, you publish in your offices or across the polling units and on INEC website or any website officially designated by INEC,” Itodo said. ﻿ He said INEC had indicated that the claims and objections exercise had been conducted across the country through physical visits to designated locations. However, he noted that the voters’ register was still unavailable on the commission’s website or any other officially designated website. “What INEC has said is that the claims and objections has been conducted across the country and what you might call manually or the one that requires physical visitation of those areas but the one online as of today, the voters’ register is not on INEC’s website or on any official website. And what the law says in Section 19 of the Act is INEC shall, which means it is compulsory,” he said. Itodo maintained that INEC was required to publish the register online in addition to displaying it at polling units, adding that the commission had failed to comply with that provision 85 days before the election. He urged the electoral body to explain why it had not published the register online, warning that its silence could undermine public confidence. “I think INEC owes it to the Nigerian voters to really make a statement as to why it has not been able to implement this part of the law. This silence does not inspire confidence, so INEC needs to explain to the people. In so far as you haven’t explained to the people and there is silence, it raises a lot of questions,” Itodo added. item.title: Fubara Promises 700 Shops At Creek Road Market By January 2027
item.description: The Rivers State Governor, Siminalayi Fubara, says the first phase of the Creek Road Market reconstruction in Old Port Harcourt Township will provide about 700 shops for traders, ease traffic congestion, and improve trading conditions. Governor Fubara stated this during an inspection of the ongoing project, where he expressed satisfaction with the quality and progress of work. He said the new market would accommodate wet and dry goods traders, particularly women currently selling along Creek Road and adjoining streets, allowing for the rehabilitation of surrounding roads. “With 700 shops, it is clear that our women who are trading along the Creek Road will be relocated, and we’ll have freer access along the road,” the Governor said. Fubara described Old Port Harcourt Township as a historic part of the city, home to elderly residents and the original inhabitants, whom he referred to as the “Aborigines.” Governor Siminalayi Fubara of Rivers State (centre). He stressed the need to restore the area’s cleanliness and dignity, noting that street trading had extended beyond Creek Road to other roads in the township. “It’s important we tidy up this road so that these traders can evacuate the major road, and the road will be free,” he said. The Governor assured that his administration would provide the necessary support to ensure the project’s timely completion, adding that the contractor had promised delivery by the end of January 2027. The project forms part of the Fubara administration’s urban renewal efforts to improve commercial activities, ease traffic movement and create a cleaner environment in Port Harcourt. item.title: Zamfara Govt Deploys Medical Personnel To Airport, Motor Parks For Ebola Screening
item.description: The Zamfara State Government has deployed medical personnel to Gusau International Airport and major motor parks across the state to screen passengers and strengthen surveillance against the spread of Ebola Virus Disease. Zamfara State Commissioner for Health, Nafisa Maradun, disclosed this while leading a medical team to flag off the screening of passengers arriving at the Gusau International Airport. Nafisa said medical personnel had also been deployed to major motor parks across the state to ensure early detection and prompt reporting of suspected cases. She noted that the screening exercise had identified a passenger with an elevated body temperature who arrived in Gusau after returning from Saudi Arabia. The state government has also directed public and private health facilities, disease surveillance officers and local government health authorities to strengthen preparedness and response measures against the disease. The Director of Public Health Services, Yusuf Abubakar, issued the directive on behalf of the Commissioner for Health during a meeting with health stakeholders and representatives of the Nigeria Customs Service, Nigeria Immigration Service and the National Union of Road Transport Workers (NURTW). Abubakar said the Customs and Immigration Services would support surveillance at border entry points, while the NURTW would assist in monitoring passengers at motor parks and alerting relevant authorities to suspected cases. He directed disease surveillance officers across the state’s 14 local government areas to notify health facilities, intensify routine and event-based surveillance, and ensure the prompt reporting of suspected cases. The Director also disclosed that the ministry had commenced temperature screening, sensitisation of frontline health workers, identification of passengers of interest and activation of response mechanisms at different levels. He further directed health facilities to strengthen screening and triage procedures, infection prevention and control, early identification of suspected cases, immediate notification and safe referral. The State Epidemiology Unit and relevant public health authorities are also expected to assess the state’s preparedness, including isolation facilities, referral arrangements, trained personnel, personal protective equipment, laboratory procedures and emergency logistics. The ministry called on relevant stakeholders to work together to strengthen surveillance and ensure strict compliance with public health guidelines to protect residents of Zamfara State and prevent the spread of the disease.
